name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 3, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:00 p.m., on February 3, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 29, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 6:15 p.m.)
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 5:17 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

Prior to the Closed Session, Dr. Samuel J. Stratton, Medical Director of the Orange County
Emergency Medical Services (EMS) Department, spoke on financial troubles and the potential
sale of Medix Ambulance Service. He also discussed his decision to appoint Doctor's Ambulance
as the backup provider should Medix be unable to respond to calls. Dr. Stratton assured the
Council that there is a plan in place and the situation is being monitored very closely to protect
the residents of Mission Viejo.

City Council Minutes  1  February 3, 2014
 CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel: Anticipated Litigation Initiation of Litigation
  Pursuant to Subdivision (c) of Section 54956.9: One Potential Case.

RECESS

At the hour of 5:32 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with four City Council Members present. Council Member
Schlicht arrived at 6:15 p.m.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Reardon

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council directed staff to provide a positive
response to a proposal from the President of Medix Ambulance to pursue a no-fault termination
of the City's contract with Medix. The Council voted unanimously with Council Member
Schlicht absent. Mr. Curley noted that if the no-fault termination does not reach closure, then
staff will commence an involuntary termination of the contract with Medix.

PRESENTATIONS

*Items P1 and P2 were taken out of order.

P2. Recognize the 2013 Employees of the Year

  Mayor Kelley presented plaques to (1) Senior Public Services Contracts Administrator Luis
  Gonzalez, City of Mission Viejo Employee of the Year; (2) Deputy Adam Sandler, Orange
  County Sheriff's Department Employee of the Year; and (3) Fire Captain Brent Anderson,
  Orange County Fire Authority Employee of the Year.

P1. Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Kelley presented certificates of commendation to "Marine of the Quarter" Lance
  Corporal Justin T. Reyes and "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Sergeant Jason M.
  Fernandez.

P3. Wounded Warriors Presentation

  The City Council received the presentation from Victor Gonzalez who thanked the Council
  for their support of the 2013 Wounded Warriors Amputee Softball Game. Mr.
  Gonzalez asked for the City's support of this year's Wounded Warriors event which will be
  held on Saturday, May 3, 2014, at the Youth Athletic Park.

City Council Minutes  2  February 3, 2014
 P4. Proclaim February 7, 2014, To Be "National Wear Red Day" in the City of Mission
  Viejo

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Dave Sanford, Member of the Passion
  Committee of the American Heart Association.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Elizabeth Busick, M.V.: announced that there will be free dental care for adults who cannot get
dental care elsewhere. The service will be provided on Saturday, February 15, 2014, at 24022
Calle de la Plata, Suite 450 in Laguna Hills and more information is available at
www.lagunasmiles.com or by calling (949) 830-0074. Mrs. Busick also encouraged residents to
check the box on their California 540 income tax form and donate to Code 402 which funds the
California Senior Legislature.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: reminded the City Council that he requested, at the last meeting, that
an RFP be issued for outside legal services but a contract was awarded to Lozano Smith instead.
Mr. Wontrobski said that no Council Member, other than Council Member Schlicht, read the
case against Lozano Smith and he stated that Mr. Curley failed to give a full and complete report
of the court findings against the firm.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 5 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and
  further reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of January 20, 2014, as
  presented.

City Council Minutes  3  February 3, 2014
 3.  Check Register Dated January 10, 2014 in the Amount of $700,831.67

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated January 17, 2014 in the Amount of $296,321.90

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  800 MHz Countywide Coordinated Communications System (CCCS) Next Generation
  Project

  Approved the Letter of Agreement for the funding of the 800 MHz CCCS Next Generation
  Project.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

7.  Banners for Active Military Personnel

  Steve Bell, Acting Director of Recreation and Community Services, presented the staff
  report.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to no
  longer consider the military banner program.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

8.  Contract to Host the 2014 International Tennis Federation (ITF) Wheelchair Doubles
  Masters

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in opposition to the City hosting the 2014 ITF Wheelchair Doubles
  Masters: Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.

  The following spoke in support of the City of Mission Viejo hosting the 2014 ITF
  Wheelchair Doubles Masters: Annette Buck, U.S. Tennis Association, Los Angeles; Jason
  Harnett, San Juan Capistrano; Steve Everett, Lakewood; Olivier Fabre, M.V.; Ryan Fabre,
  M.V.; and David Wagner, San Diego.

City Council Minutes  4  February 3, 2014
   Steve Bell, Acting Director of Recreation and Community Services, answered the City
  Council Members questions.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to (1) direct staff to
  negotiate contract terms with the ITF for hosting the 2014 Wheelchair Doubles Masters;
  and (2) authorize the City Manager to execute the contract.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

5.  Amendment to Library Hours for 2014 Calendar Year

  Council Member Schlicht noted that she will be voting no because she feels that the library
  should stay open during the holidays because it is a public facility.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to table the
  item and direct staff to return the matter, along with library holiday attendance numbers, for
  review and consideration at a future City Council Meeting.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

9.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: reported that there have been two major developments related
  to the OCFA. The State EMS Agency in Sacramento has directed that the ambulance
  transport RFP cannot be issued and administered by the OCFA and he stated that that is a
  gigantic step forward for the public. Mr. Wontrobski also reported that the Orange County
  Board of Supervisors rejected the court filing for the OCFA's JPA equitable adjustment
  amendment which the City of Mission Viejo approved against his opposition.

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.
City Council Minutes  5  February 3, 2014
 10. Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that the Orange County Fire Authority is undergoing major
reform and there are issues and irregularities that have been brought to light yet at Council
Meetings, members of the public, the City Attorney and staff have not learned of these
issues. Mr. Wontrobski outlined several recent decisions from the State relative to OCFA.

Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay discussed staff's plans to light city hall in red for National
Heart Association month. The lights will be turned on at the Civic Center on Friday, February 7
and will remain throughout the month. Mr. Rattay further announced that the American Heart
Association is hosting a free CPR class on February 18, 2014, from 5:00 to 8:35 p.m. in the
Saddleback Room at city hall for up to 35 students and more information is available on the
City's website.

City Manager Wilberg responded to questions about the City's 2013 letter to the Orange County
Board of Supervisors objecting to the County's plan to take over the ambulance selection
process.

The Council Members and staff discussed the subject of the State and County attempts to take
away local control.

City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Bill Curley reminded the Council of his comments at the last meeting regarding
the "sex offenders in parks" ordinance and his recommendation to maintain the status quo with
that ordinance. Mr. Curley informed the City Council that the City has received a letter from the
ACLU's California Reform Sex Offenders Law Group requesting the immediate repeal of the
City's sex offender ordinance. Mr. Curley noted that he will be talking to the firm about the letter
and he maintained his previous recommendation to keep the ordinance on the books and not
enforce it until there is a final judicial decision on the County matter.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

11. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented
  in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

City Council Minutes  6  February 3, 2014
 Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon announced that she received a letter from the Assistance League of
Saddleback Valley thanking the City for its generous donation of $6,500. The donation will
enable the Assistance League to continue funding programs such as Operation School Bell which
clothes school age children and Council Member Reardon noted that the money the City donated
stays in Mission Viejo. She also recognized and congratulated La Paz Intermediate School on
being declared a Model School for the third year in a row. Council Member Reardon recognized
resident Sharon Campbell for her hard work in eliminating Mello-Roos taxes and she
congratulated Eileen Gonzalez, the wife of Wounded Warriors organizer Victor Gonzalez, for
beating cancer and she stated that it was good to see her healthy tonight. Council Member
Reardon discussed her attendance at the OCFA Best and the Bravest awards. She stated that it
was so nice to hear what OCFA is doing and she enjoyed sitting with firefighter Tim Merchant's
family and getting to know them. She also attended the Elks Club Law Enforcement and
Firefighter Appreciation Awards Dinner where Deputy Adam Sandler was honored by Lt.
NewMyer. Lastly, Council Member Reardon discussed former OSCD employee Tammy
Descoteaux and her history with the Sheriff's Department. Although retired now, Mrs.
Descoteaux will be presenting an interactive workshop for adults and teens on face to face
communication. The program will be held on Wednesday, February 12 from 7:00 to 9:00 p.m. at
the Murray Community Center and she encouraged anyone who is having trouble with their
teenagers to take the class and register with Police Services by calling (949) 470-8433.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht congratulated the wheelchair tennis players and stated that they
deserve the accolades for overcoming their disability and showing the spirit of man. She also
commended Brad Parks who created wheelchair tennis 25 years ago. Council Member Schlicht
stated that she doesn't think that the residents of Mission Viejo, as taxpayers, need to be funding
wheelchair tennis at the level they did (in 2013.) She said that staff failed to properly manage
the costs which were over $34,000 a day for an event that generated less than $10,000 in ticket
sales. She noted that she has submitted her comments for the public record and she mentioned
that it was ironic that the newspaper just covered a Costa Mesa event that had significant cost
overruns. In that case an audit revealed that protocols were not followed and, as a result, Costa
Mesa has implemented new procedures that are not allowed to be breached without
consequences. Council Member Schlicht stated that the wheelchair tennis event received in-kind
sponsorships of $97,731 but she feels that the value of in-kind donations is fluid and hard to pin
down. She also said that the agenda report summary (for item 8) is incomplete because certain
details were not included and one can massage numbers to make them go either way. Council
Member Schlicht noted that this year's wheelchair tennis event is projected to cost about $60,000
less but it wasn't disclosed that last year's event included both a singles and doubles tournament
and this year's event will only be doubles. She reiterated that she feels there was gross
overspending and the event has no benefit to the community. Council Member Schlicht stated
that the City funded a first-class vacation for 36 tennis players, their coaches, the ITF staff,
sponsors and guests and the event cannot be compared to the Target Symphony or all the
programs for kids which, she said, have a direct benefit to the community. Council Member

City Council Minutes  7  February 3, 2014
 Schlicht concluded her comments with a favorite quote: "It is dangerous to be right when
government is wrong."

Council Member Ury

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley thanked the Elks Club for honoring standout police officers and firefighters every
year and she congratulated Captain Jon Walla and Deputy Adam Sandler on their awards. She
also discussed her attendance at a Mayor's Roundtable hosted by Supervisor Pat Bates which
focused on senior issues and upcoming senior events. Mayor Kelley asked members of the
public to contact her if they are interested in serving on the Relay for Life Committee. She noted
that she served on the Committee for 10 years, helping to raise funds for the American Cancer
Society and that the committee is looking for new members. Meetings are held on the third
Wednesday of every month with the next meeting on February 19 at 7:00 p.m. at the Murray
Center. Mayor Kelley concluded her comments by announcing that the Community of Character
word for the month of February is unity and the movie of character, Lincoln, will be shown in
the Council Chamber on Sunday, February 16, 2014, at 2:00 p.m.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:00 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of OCFA Firefighter Apparatus
Engineer Greg Hennessey, to Monday, February 17, 2014, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of February 17, 2014

City Council Minutes  8  February 3, 2014
